title: The Crooked Oath Anew
premise: Sebastian Winterbourne steals memories for a living in Vellharrow, a city where magic was outlawed and memory itself became contraband. When a mute child named Ives arrives at her door speaking a language older than any kingdom, Sebastian discovers the girl carries the unbinding word for the thing that has worn King Aldric's crown for seven years — the same years Sebastian's own stolen memories have been missing. Hunted by the Crown's mnemonic inquisitors and shadowed by the oathbreaker who taught her her trade, Sebastian must gather the scattered fragments of her past to complete the unbinding before the coronation renewal rite seals the king to his parasite forever. In the end she sacrifices her recovered memories of found family to speak the word truly, choosing to rebuild those bonds anew rather than keep them as possessions.
about_author: Gideon Coldharbour is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated letters in a coastal city's records office before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about what people carry, what they bury, and what they refuse to inherit.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Hours
chapters.summary: Sebastian lifts a dying woman's happiest hour from a locket and sells it in the night market, establishing her trade and her careful loneliness. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: competence masking grief; she cannot remember why she flinches at church bells.

chapters.title: A Knock Older Than Doors
chapters.summary: A child appears at Sebastian's garret door, silent except for words in a language no one living should know. The girl's presence makes Sebastian's memory-charms curdle and rot. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: wary wonder; the first crack in seven years of routine.

chapters.title: What the Charms Remember
chapters.summary: Sebastian consults Quill, a fence of magical goods, who identifies the child's speech as Oathscript — the tongue in which binding magic was originally sworn. Inquisitors raid the market behind them. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: dread; the past is not dead, only priced.

chapters.title: The King Who Smiles Wrong
chapters.summary: At a public audience, Sebastian watches King Aldric greet petitioners and notices he never blinks during the anthem. A courtier with hollow eyes marks her face in the crowd. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: cold recognition; the crown is a mouth.

chapters.title: Ives
chapters.summary: Sebastian names the child Ives and begins teaching her thieves' signs; Ives teaches back, drawing Oathscript glyphs that make Sebastian's missing years ache like a pulled tooth. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: tenderness arriving uninvited; found family begins as inconvenience.

chapters.title: The Mnemonist's Ledger
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Serane Corvane interrogates Quill and finds Sebastian's name in a seven-year-old ledger of unsanctioned extractions — dated the week Sebastian's own memories vanished. POV: Serane. Emotional beat: dutiful suspicion curdling into doubt about what she serves.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sold Himself Twice
chapters.summary: Sebastian seeks her old teacher, Dree Halloway, an oathbreaker living under a false death. Dree recognizes Ives's glyphs and goes white: they are the counter-word to a royal binding. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: bitter reunion; mentors are just debts with faces.

chapters.title: Seven Years Missing
chapters.summary: Dree reveals Sebastian sold her own memories willingly to hide something — and refuses to say what, claiming the price of telling is worse than the price of ignorance. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: fury and vertigo; she was the architect of her own amnesia.

chapters.title: The Renewal Rite
chapters.summary: Serane witnesses the private coronation renewal ceremony and sees the king's shadow move independently, drinking from a chalice of rendered memory. She files no report. POV: Serane. Emotional beat: horror and complicity; knowing is the first treason.

chapters.title: Market of Teeth
chapters.summary: To fund their flight, Sebastian brokers a dangerous extraction from a guildmaster's mind and nearly loses herself inside it; Ives pulls her out using Oathscript instinctively. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: terror and gratitude; the child is saving her in ways she can't repay.

chapters.title: Hollow Eyes
chapters.summary: The courtier from the audience finds them; in the fight, Sebastian learns the man is a vessel like the king — a person long since emptied and worn. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: revulsion and pity; the enemy is also a victim wearing a stolen face.

chapters.title: Dree's Confession
chapters.summary: Cornered by inquisitors, Dree trades truth for time: seven years ago he helped bind the king, and Sebastian — then his apprentice — carried the binding knife. Her sold memories contain the unbinding's second half. POV: Dree. Emotional beat: shame finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: The Vault of Given Things
chapters.summary: Sebastian traces her sold memories to the Crown repository beneath the palace, where confiscated magic is stored. Serane, off-ledger, leaves the service entrance unlocked — an act of quiet defection. POV: Serane. Emotional beat: treachery as conscience; doors open both ways.

chapters.title: Everything I Paid
chapters.summary: Sebastian recovers a single vial of her own memory and relives the binding night: she held the knife, weeping, while Dree swore the crooked oath that caged the parasite — imperfectly. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: devastating self-knowledge; she chose this once already.

chapters.title: Why the Child Came
chapters.summary: Ives speaks her first common-tongue words: she is the residue of the binding, the part of the oath that refused to hold, given flesh to finish or undo it. POV: Ives (rendered through Sebastian). Emotional beat: heartbreak; the family she loves is a spell with legs.

chapters.title: Corvane's Choice
chapters.summary: Serane is caught aiding them and must choose: burn the evidence and her career, or burn the children. She burns the ledger instead and joins them. POV: Serane. Emotional beat: liberation through ruin; an oath kept by breaking it.

chapters.title: The Crooked Oath Anew
chapters.summary: In the undercroft, Dree proposes re-swearing the original binding correctly rather than unbinding it — safer, but it would erase Ives entirely. Sebastian refuses. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: moral rupture; safety bought with a child's life is just theft with better manners.

chapters.title: Palace of Worn Faces
chapters.summary: The four infiltrate the renewal rite through the servant veins of the palace, passing vessels who smile without blinking. Dree is taken covering their retreat. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into resolve; some debts can only be paid forward.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Before the assembled court, the parasite reveals itself through the king's mouth, offering Sebastian her full memories back if she renews the oath. It shows her the found family she forgot — including a version where Ives never existed. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: temptation at its most intimate.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Word
chapters.summary: At the climax, Sebastian realizes the word requires a speaker with nothing left to lose — so she gives up every recovered memory, holding Ives's hand as they speak Oathscript together. The crown cracks; the king collapses, freed and ancient. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship; she empties herself to end a theft.

chapters.title: Strangers at the Door
chapters.summary: Aftermath: Sebastian remembers nothing of the last weeks. Ives stands at her garret door again, a stranger — but her hand remembers how to sign 'stay.' Serane arrives with bread and a lie about being an old friend. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: tender devastation; love outlasting its evidence.

chapters.title: Anew
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the city breathes under a regency council; magic remains outlawed but memory-thieves are quietly pardoned. Sebastian begins stealing nothing and keeping everything, rebuilding a family from scratch with people who grieve her loss alongside her. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: inheritance reversed; what we choose twice is truly ours.
